html:
The largest building in Teotihuacan, the great city of the Valley of Mexico, finished around 200 CE. It stands about 65 metres high on the east side of the Avenue of the Dead, between the Pyramid of the Moon and the Ciudadela, and is one of the largest structures built in the ancient Americas.

It was made of rubble and earth faced with stone, once covered in painted plaster. Under it lies a long cave or tunnel that ends in chambers; for the builders this was likely a sacred place of origin, and the pyramid was raised over it on purpose.

The name is not original. The Aztecs, who found the city in ruins centuries later, called it Teotihuacan, "where the gods were made", and named its buildings. They believed the sun of the present age was born there. Mexican archaeologists rebuilt much of the pyramid in the early 1900s, removing a layer of its surface.
